title: Exchange cells with a push: orientation, small deviations, mutual costs

key_results.statement: $J>0$, field alone, every $S$, cubic torus or ring of even side: the lowest eigenvector is unique, a total-spin singlet, unchanged by every common rotation, with $\langle\mathbf S_x\rangle=0$.
$J<0$, field alone: lowest eigenvalue $JS^2DN$, $(2NS+1)$-fold degenerate; no lowest eigenvector is unchanged by all common rotations.

$J<0$ with the push: the product state is the unique lowest eigenvector and $\langle\mathbf n\cdot\mathbf S_x\rangle=S$ exactly for every $x$, $L$, $S$, $h_p>0$, both graphs and both orders of limits.
$J>0$, order $h_p\to0$ at fixed $L$, then $L\to\infty$: $m(x)=O(h_p)\to0$ for every $S$ on both graphs (exact).

Leading order in $1/S$ about the orientation set by the push: $C=E_0+\frac12\sum_{\alpha=1,2}q^{(\alpha)T}(JS\Delta+h_pP_h)q^{(\alpha)}+O(J)$ with $q^{(\alpha)}_x=\epsilon_x\mathbf e_\alpha\cdot\mathbf S_x/\sqrt S$, $[q^{(1)}_x,q^{(2)}_y]=i\epsilon_x\delta_{xy}$, valid while $\langle n_x\rangle\ll S$.
The expansion in $1/S$ with the push requires $Nh_pS\gg zJ$ (zero modes pinned): met in the order $L\to\infty$ first, violated in the order $h_p\to0$ at fixed $L$.
Cubic torus, $J>0$, order $L\to\infty$, $R\to\infty$, then $h_p\to0$: $m(x)\to\epsilon_h[S-\Delta S_3+O(1/S)]$ with $\Delta S_3=\frac12[\int(1-\gamma_k^2)^{-1/2}-1]=0.0784$, independent of $h_p>0$.
Ring (control): $m(R)=S-\frac1\pi\ln R+O(1)+O(1/S)$; the first correction is not uniform in $R$ and the expansion in $1/S$ does not decide the order $L\to\infty$, $R\to\infty$ at any $S$.

Exact diagonalization ($S=\frac12$ rings $L\le20$ and one 16-object cubic cluster, $S=1$ rings $L\le12$): $m_{\rm far}$ is linear in $h_p\to0$ at fixed size and on rings with $h_p\ge J$ falls monotonically with $L$; for $S=\frac12$ on the cubic torus the order $L\to\infty$, $R\to\infty$ is undecided at these sizes.

Identification at leading order in $1/S$: two conjugate copies $q^{(\alpha)}$ with the 05-anchor matrix $A=JS\Delta+h_pP_h$, $\kappa_h=JS$, $\kappa_a=h_p$, $g_s=\epsilon_{x_s}\sqrt S g(\mathbf m\cdot\mathbf e_\alpha)$, exact for static results; kinetic matrix $EAE$ instead of $\mathbb 1$; for wavelengths $\gg1$ two independent copies of the 05-anchor field with $\kappa_h=2zJ^2S^2$, $\kappa_a=2zJSh_p$, $g_s=\epsilon_{x_s}S\sqrt{2zJ}g(\mathbf m\cdot\mathbf e_\alpha)$.
Conditions of (8.10): $\Delta S_3\ll S$, $Nh_pS\gg zJ$, $|g|\ll h_p$, $|g|\ll JS$; on the ring also $\frac1\pi\ln d\ll S$ and $|g|d\ll JS$ at the distances used.

Under (8.10), (8.11): (5.3) with the anchor, (5.8), (5.10), (5.11), (5.14), (5.15) hold; the outcome no lowest eigenvector of (5.3)–(5.6) fails because one exists, and unbounded outcomes become bounded rotations of the orientation; next order in $1/S$ changes coefficients by relative $O(1/S)$.

Transverse direction sources, order $g_1g_2$, leading order in $1/S$, every $L$, both graphs: $\mathcal E^\perp_{12}=-S\epsilon_{x_1}\epsilon_{x_2}g_1g_2(\mathbf m_1^\perp\cdot\mathbf m_2^\perp)G_a(x_1,x_2)$.

Cubic torus, order $L\to\infty$, distances to $h\to\infty$, then $r\to\infty$: separation part $-\epsilon_{x_1}\epsilon_{x_2}g_1g_2(\mathbf m_1^\perp\cdot\mathbf m_2^\perp)c_1c_2/(4\pi Jr)$ ($c_i=1$ single object, $2$ cell): a long-range mark of order $S^0$; it vanishes for a source at $h$ or $\mathbf m_1^\perp\cdot\mathbf m_2^\perp=0$.

Along-$\mathbf n$ direction sources: mutual cost $-\epsilon_{x_1}\epsilon_{x_2}g_1g_2(\mathbf m_1\cdot\mathbf n)(\mathbf m_2\cdot\mathbf n)c_1c_2\kappa_\parallel/(JSr^3)$, $\kappa_\parallel=\sqrt3/(16\pi^3)$, order $g_1g_2/(JS)$: no long-range mark.

Changed link (R2): $-\frac{\sqrt3}{8\pi^3}\frac{\delta_1\delta_2S}{Jr^7}a$ with $a=\frac{43}6+\frac52\epsilon_1\epsilon_2$ (links parallel to $\mathbf r$) or $\frac43-\frac5{12}\epsilon_1\epsilon_2$ (links perpendicular), order $\delta_1\delta_2S/J$, attractive in both geometries for $\delta_1\delta_2>0$: no long-range mark.

Held spin (R1): $-|g'_1g'_2|s_{b_1}s_{b_2}\kappa_\parallel/(JSr^3)$ for $1\ll r\ll\ell_b=\sqrt{2z}J/|g'|$; $\frac{3\sqrt3}{8\pi^3}\frac JS\sigma_1\sigma_2\epsilon_{x_1}\epsilon_{x_2}r^{-5}$ with $\sigma_i=-s_{b_i}{\rm sgn}\,g'_i$ for $r\gg\ell_b$ (the law for $r\to\infty$ last): no long-range mark.

Without a push: direction sources with $\mathbf h_{\rm eff}\ne0$ fix the orientation $-\mathbf h_{\rm eff}/|\mathbf h_{\rm eff}|$ and their $1/r$ part becomes repulsive, $+c_1^2g_1^2|\mathbf m_1^\perp|^2/(4\pi Jr)$, absent for parallel $\mathbf m$ with $\mathbf h_{\rm eff}\ne0$; relation sources fix no orientation (Lieb–Mattis) and (8.17), (8.18) are unchanged as $L\to\infty$.

open_issues: For S = 1/2 on the cubic torus the persistence of the orientation far from the push is undecided: one cluster of 16 objects.
On the ring the methods used do not decide m(x) far from the push; exact diagonalization only shows a decrease with L for L ≤ 20.
The next order in 1/S of (8.13)–(8.18) is not computed; survival of the 1/r law of (8.14) at all orders is not proven.
The crossover of (8.18) near r ~ ℓ_b and the corrections near the push are not computed; (8.17) is evaluated for two link geometries only.
The rotor regime N h_p S ~ zJ between the two orders of item 1(b) is not computed.

consistency_checks.check: S → ∞ of item 1(b): m/S → 1, the product state with staggered orientation; exact product state for J < 0
Identification against (5.15): 4πr ĝ_∞(r) → 1 on the lattice; R2 vertex summed over link directions equals the energy density of the copy
Dimensions and S-scaling of all mutual costs: (vertex)² / (level spacing JS)
